Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I see we have the core team from Orpheus on, uh, so quick intros — i'm Maya from Redwood, AE; liam is our solutions engineer, riley product.
[00:18] Rajiv (CTO): hey, rajiv here. short on time so appreciate a practical walkthrough. main ask is how we can get down to predictable unit costs while hitting 120ms p95 for our chat assistants.
[00:32] Liam (SE): cool, that's helpful — can you confirm current throughput? peak qps, average session length?
[00:40] Sofia (ML Eng): average qps is 18, peaks at 95 during biz hours, average request sequence is ~220 tokens, sometimes sessions hit 700 tokens for multi-turn.
[00:55] Derek (Platform): and we're on AWS in us-east-1, VPC controlled, egress policies strict, we use AWS KMS for keys.
[01:08] Maya: perfect. we'll focus on three levers: batching/concurrency, prefix (KV) caching, and routing to smaller quantized variants for lower latency/cost. liam, we'll flip to the console?
[01:22] Liam: yes, sharing screen now — bear with the slide deck, then we'll run the Optimize sim with Orpheus traffic shape.
[01:38] [screen share noises / brief pause]
[01:46] Liam: ok in the Optimize tab — top left you can load traffic traces; riley uploaded an anonymized trace matching the qps you mentioned. we run the sim for a set of policies: aggressive batching, conservative batching, and session-affinity + prefix cache.
[02:05] Sofia: what's the default batch size here? how does continuous batching interact with latency?
[02:12] Liam: default is dynamic up to 64 tokens per microbatch for this model family; continuous batching tries to fill smaller microbatches within a latency budget — you can set a 120ms p95 target and it'll adapt. note sometimes transcripts show KV as K V cache — that's an autosub artifact.
[02:33] Rajiv: ha, ok — can you show a concrete cost delta between enabling prefix cache v no cache?
[02:38] Liam: sure. running the sim now — baseline: no prefix cache, conservative batching. baseline unit cost estimate: $0.017 per generated token equivalent (simulated).
[02:52] [clicks]
[02:56] Liam: enable prefix cache with 12-hour TTL, lookahead prefetch on session start — re-running sim...
[03:08] Liam: results: token-equivalent cost drops ~31%, effective throughput increases because KV hits short-circuit several decoder steps. p95 latency moves from 145ms to 128ms in this trace because prefix cache avoids full decoding for repeated prompts.
[03:26] Sofia: interesting — are there hit-rate assumptions baked in? our prompt variance is higher for support flows.
[03:33] Liam: yes we modeled a 42% cache hit-rate in the sim based on your histogram riley uploaded. if hit-rate drops to 20% savings shrink to ~12%. console shows a slider for hit-rate sensitivity.
[03:46] Rajiv: what about KV eviction and storage cost? we don't want the cache to balloon.
[03:52] Liam: good point — in the sim we set a bounded KV store with LRU, TTL, and per-customer partitioning. storage is negligible compared to GPU tokens but we do include storage egress in the total. you can see per-GB cost shown in the breakdown.
[04:10] Amira (Security): can you clarify data at rest encryption and KMS integration for KV? we need to present to compliance.
[04:18] Maya: yes — for Private/Dedicated we support customer KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs for all calls. we'll share the SOC2 + KMS config doc in the follow-ups.
[04:30] [laughter / cross-talk]
[04:38] Liam: next, routing policy example — you can prefer a quantized 8-bit variant for lower cost, but we test quality delta on your eval set. the console flags when quality drop > 2% BLEU-equivalent or failure cases.
[04:55] Sofia: what's the failover plan if the cheaper variant regresses on a subset?
[04:59] Liam: stateful routing — we keep a small canary percentage and fallback automatically on error or quality drift. also console supports per-customer routing override for critical personas.
[05:10] Derek: latency concerns — when you do batching aggressively, doesn't tail latency spike? our SLA must be 120ms p95.
[05:18] Liam: batching trades throughput for latency — the Optimize sim lets you set a strict p95 SLO and it dynamically reduces batching when latency is threatened; the concurrency controller can also spin up dedicated capacity to meet p95 at cost.
[05:34] Rajiv: show us a scenario where we preserve p95 and reduce cost by at least 20%.
[05:39] Liam: run scenario: sessionization enabled, prefix cache TTL 6h, small prefetch window, set p95 target 120ms. running...
[05:52] Liam: outcome: cost -22% with p95=119ms on this workload, concurrency increased 12% at peak but overall GPU hours lower due to cache hits.
[06:05] Sofia: ok but those numbers feel optimistic — what's the sensitivity to burstiness? we have sudden spikes from marketing pushes.
[06:12] Liam: we model burst policy — you can set a burst buffer on dedicated tiers that allows short hot spikes without immediate autoscale. for hosted we'd route overflow to a higher-cost fallback region.
[06:25] Rajiv: routing to regions — does that increase latency unpredictably?
[06:29] Maya: it's policy-based. low-latency customers stay in region; overflows go to the nearest compatible region which adds maybe 20-40ms — we surface that in the sim and you can choose to disable cross-region overflow for strict p95.
[06:44] [pause]
[06:50] Riley (Product): i'd like to flag a real-world tip — often a small amount of prompt engineering saves more than aggressive batch tuning. adding a fixed system prompt that collapses repetitive context increases KV hit-rate.
[07:04] Sofia: we've experimented with prompt compaction, but it degraded few-shot performance; where do we compromise?
[07:11] Liam: console's evals tab runs your prompt suite across model variants under the proposed policies — it highlights failing prompts so you can decide which to keep.
[07:23] Rajiv: security again, what about audit logs and redaction for PII in cache entries?
[07:30] Amira: yes, we can't keep unredacted PII in KV.
[07:34] Maya: we support per-keyredaction hooks and a redaction pipeline so that prefix cache stores only tokenized, hashed contexts or redacted strings; the policy can be customer-controlled. we'll send the redaction doc.
[07:48] Derek: on networking — if we do Private (VPC) deployment, what's involved for peering? downtime?
[07:55] Liam: non-disruptive — we provision a customer VPC endpoint, peering negotiated via CloudFormation; typical lead time is 2-3 business days for standard accounts; we'll list required CIDR and security group rules.
[08:10] [background noise]
[08:16] Sofia: back to numbers — can we get a CSV export of the sim with per-route cost breakdown?
[08:21] Maya: yes, the console exports per-route, per-model breakdown; i'll share a pre-filled CSV for your traffic mix.
[08:31] [typing noises]
[08:38] Liam: one nuance — KV hit-rate is highly correlated with session affinity. if you distribute sessions across many nodes without sticky session or global session service, hits drop. we model two approaches: client-side sticky identifiers vs server-side session-store.
[08:59] Rajiv: we're leaning to server-side session-store for fault-tolerance. how much overhead does that add?
[09:05] Liam: marginal; session-store adds network hops but keeps affinity when a node crashes — the sim adds ~6ms average per request but KV hit-rate retention offsets that by 20% token cost reduction in good cases.
[09:20] Sofia: curious about long-tail sequences — some flows have 1,200 tokens across a support transcript; how does prefetch help there?
[09:27] Liam: lookahead prefetch grabs likely horizon tokens when the session has high repeat structure; it amortizes KV costs across the long tail. in practice it reduces decoder steps for repeated templates.
[09:40] Rajiv: ok, how does pricing show up for Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
[09:47] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable hourly commitments with discounts on unit cost — in that scenario the sim shows lower per-token cost on steady load but less flexibility on large marketing spikes. Hosted is elastic but higher per-token when sustained high qps. we'll include a side-by-side in the spreadsheet.
[10:05] Derek: can we do a short live micro-benchmark? maybe replay 10k requests from a trace to see p95 in real time?
[10:13] Liam: yes we have a sandbox runner that replays your trace against our staging cluster with KV enabled; we can run a short replay now but it takes ~12 minutes for a 10k trace. do you want to kick it off?
[10:24] Rajiv: let's do a smaller 2k replay now for quick visibility.
[10:28] [brief pause]
[10:32] [replay starts, subtle audio overlay]
[10:36] Liam: replay running — initial p95 reported 135ms no cache, enabling prefix cache now.
[10:45] Sofia: seeing throughput bump already.
[10:50] Liam: cache enabled — p95 drops to 121ms, token cost proxy drops ~28% in the run. these are staging numbers with our modest staging hardware but directionally useful.
[11:02] Rajiv: that's promising. do we have an SLO breach in this run?
[11:06] Liam: a few anomalous tails at minute 4 during a burst — console shows a tail analysis and root cause trace pointing to a cold KV partition miss. we can pre-warm partitions in your sandbox.
[11:20] Maya: we'll configure pre-warm for critical routes in the pilot.
[11:25] [short silence]
[11:30] Amira: what about logging retention and log access for audits? we need 12 months retention for events and ability to export for auditors.
[11:39] Maya: do-able — add-on retention package provides 12–24 month logs, and exports via S3 with access controls; we'll include pricing for that in the follow-up.
[11:50] Riley (Product): one more product note — the Optimize sim supports multi-variant rollouts where you specify a quality threshold and it will automatically route traffic away from variants that fall below. that protects production quality.
[12:04] Rajiv: good. last question — can we simulate 'marketing spike' cost if we disable expensive fallback and instead allow some degraded responses?
[12:13] Liam: yes, the sim has a policy knob: degrade-mode vs overflow-mode. degrade-mode returns shorter completions or summary tokens to preserve p95; overflow-mode routes to higher-cost capacity. show degrade-mode now — cost reduced but quality metric drops 5 points on your eval.
[12:34] Sofia: that may be acceptable for low-value flows. we need to tag routes by persona.
[12:39] Maya: the console supports per-route tags and persona-based policies. you can set critical flows to strict p95 and no degrade.
[12:47] [wrap-up begins]
[12:50] Maya: recap — we saw a scenario with ~22–31% cost reduction using prefix cache + sessionization and tuned batching while preserving p95 in the sim. next steps: orchard of action items — we'll send the sandbox, SOC2 & KMS docs, and the CSV cost model export.
[13:06] Rajiv: sounds good. timeline: if sandbox starts early November we can run pilot for two weeks and then decide Dedicated/reserved commit by mid-November.
[13:16] Maya: perfect — we'll aim to provision the sandbox by Nov 2.
[13:20] Sofia: i'll send the traffic histograms and the edge cases we saw in the field by Friday.
[13:26] Derek: i'll check with infra on VPC peering constraints and share the network team contact.
[13:32] Amira: i'll look for the redaction sample and confirm PII policy.
[13:36] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the sim link and spreadsheet within 48 hours.
